purpose: where the Databento decode pipeline bottlenecks on this machine, and therefore what an external drive must sustain to avoid idling the CPU. Not a study; opens and closes nothing.

machine.internal_disk: KIOXIA EXCERIA PLUS G3, 932 GB NVMe

payload.what: real market bars from data/fixtures/index_extended_15m_raw.csv.gz packed into the exact 56-byte DBN OHLCV record layout, tiled to 512 MB

finding: zstd decompression is the bottleneck, not parsing. numpy parse runs 12x faster than zstd decompress, so the DBN format itself costs almost nothing to read. One worker consumes 254 MB/s of COMPRESSED disk read.
implication_for_hardware: a 10 Gbps USB enclosure delivers about 1,000 MB/s and would saturate at 4 of 12 physical cores, idling two thirds of the CPU. Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 at roughly 3,000 MB/s feeds 12 workers. This is the floor, not a luxury.
why_the_disk_is_in_the_critical_path: 31.7 GB of RAM against a roughly 200 GiB one-minute universe uncompressed. The panel cannot be held in memory, so studies stream from disk rather than loading once.
caveats: the internal NVMe read figure of 2,725 MB/s was measured on a warm page cache and is NOT a clean device measurement; the write figure of 592 MB/s is the more honest of the two
measured on OHLCV records, the most compressible schema here. MBO and MBP-1 records compress differently and their per-core decode rate was not measured
single-threaded. Multi-worker scaling was inferred by multiplication, not measured, and real scaling will fall short of linear
